items.followUp: A 5 kg load is raised through a vertical height of 4 m. Calculate the work done against gravity. Take g = 10 m s⁻².

rubric.why: The total vertical height is needed in metres before calculating the work.
rubric.description: Finds the total height as 3.6 m.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct total height in metres.

rubric.why: Work against gravity is calculated using the mass, gravitational field strength, and vertical height.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct formula.

rubric.why: The given values must be substituted into the formula using SI units.
rubric.description: Substitutes m = 10 kg, g = 10 m s⁻², and h = 3.6 m.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct substitution.

rubric.why: The work must be calculated correctly and reported with its SI unit.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for 360 and 1 mark for the unit joule (J).

modelAnswer: Given: mass, m = 10 kg; number of steps = 18; height of each step = 20 cm = 0.20 m; g = 10 m s⁻².
Work done against gravity, W = mgh.
W = 10 kg × 10 m s⁻² × 3.6 m = 360 kg m² s⁻².

items.followUp: Explain how a hydraulic lift multiplies force using Pascal's law.

rubric.why: Pascal's law is the principle on which the hydraulic press works.
rubric.description: States that pressure applied to an enclosed liquid is transmitted equally in all directions.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the key idea of Pascal's law.

rubric.why: The press requires two differently sized pistons connected by liquid.
rubric.description: Identifies two pistons of different areas connected by an enclosed liquid.

rubric.why: Equal pressure at the pistons gives the force-area relationship.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct pressure relation.

rubric.why: The different piston areas explain how the press multiplies force.
rubric.description: Explains that a small force on the smaller piston produces a larger force on the larger piston.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining the force multiplication.

modelAnswer: Pascal's law states that pressure applied to an enclosed liquid is transmitted equally in all directions.
A hydraulic press consists of two pistons of different areas connected by an enclosed liquid.
If forces F1 and F2 act on pistons of areas A1 and A2, respectively, then F1/A1 = F2/A2.
A small force applied to the smaller piston therefore produces a larger force on the larger piston.

rubric.why: This identifies both the subject of plasma physics and what plasma consists of.
rubric.description: Defines plasma physics as the branch of physics that studies plasma, a gas of charged particles.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the study of plasma and its charged-particle nature.

rubric.why: This identifies geophysics with the physical study of the Earth.
rubric.description: Defines geophysics as the application of physics to the study of the Earth and its physical properties.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking physics with the study of the Earth.

modelAnswer: Plasma physics is the branch of physics that studies plasma, a gas of charged particles.
Geophysics is the application of physics to the study of the Earth and its physical properties.
